# Historical Go implementation reference

The Go implementation was retired from the working tree at the project owner's
request on 2026-09-08. The current implementation is the Bun/TypeScript monorepo.
**Removal does not establish feature parity.** This is a historical feature and
implementation reference for completing that migration, not documentation of
capabilities already available in Bun.

The exact source is preserved in Git at
[`2567a7a7468ef2a1591e289f43d62b78b5c9679a`](https://github.com/abdul-hamid-achik/local-agent/tree/2567a7a7468ef2a1591e289f43d62b78b5c9679a).
The final inventory identifies every removed tracked file and its SHA-256.
Retrieve any implementation or test without restoring the old build:

```sh
git show 2567a7a7468ef2a1591e289f43d62b78b5c9679a:internal/agent/loop.go
```

## How to use this reference

1. Interface, configuration, TUI, providers, MCP and skills.
2. Runtime tools, authority, execution, verification and context.
3. Sessions, storage, goals, recovery, memory and experts.
4. Exact historical schema, keyboard, tool and command contracts.
5. Original product manual and build/configuration examples.
6. Complete file, function/type and test inventory.

The semantic sections explain behavior. Exact contracts and source references
resolve detail or ambiguity; a declaration or passing unit contract alone does
not prove an end-to-end feature was wired. Historical public modes are NORMAL,
PLAN and AUTO; internal AskToolPolicy/BuildToolPolicy names are separate catalog
policies, and YOLO/skip-approvals is an approval policy rather than a new TUI mode.

## Current migration boundary

Bun currently supplies the three presentations, Ollama/Chalupa admission, reads,
exact edits, argv commands, explicitly configured MCP tools and optional durable
sessions. It does not yet provide the full Go tools/flags/commands, skills and
profile behavior, compaction, reconciliation, goals, memory, expert execution or
standalone release distribution. Historical Go configurations and databases are
not silently accepted by the new client. Retired Go release automation is not a
Bun distribution pipeline. These are remaining requirements, not removed goals.

The public website stays under `docs/`; its historical-release scope is labeled.
The internal framework remains independently extractable from `packages/vue-tui`.

# Historical Go CLI interface and architecture

This inventory is based on commit `2567a7a7468ef2a1591e289f43d62b78b5c9679a` (`feat: add remote Ollama profiles and streamline terminal interactions`). It describes source and tests at that commit; comments and roadmap language are marked as planned where they describe future work.

## Invocation and command surface

`cmd/local-agent/main.go` dispatches subcommands before root flag parsing: `init`, `logs`, `goal`, `execution`, `session`, and `help`. Root help also lists these commands. `--version` exits before configuration/runtime initialization. Unknown positional arguments fail with exit code 2.

Root flags in `cmd/local-agent/cli_help.go` and `root_options.go`:

- `-p, --prompt TEXT`: one non-interactive prompt, print response, exit.
- `--tools names`: comma-separated built-in tool allowlist for headless mode.
- `--mode normal|plan|auto`: headless authority, default `normal`.
- `--auto`, `--plan`: prompt-required mode shortcuts.
- `--skip-approvals`: suppress approval prompts while retaining host/scope/tool boundaries.
- `--json`: one machine-readable turn receipt; requires prompt.
- `--run-id`, `--turn-id`, `--actor`: external receipt identity labels; require prompt.
- `--resume ID|latest`: restore an interactive saved session.
- `--model`, `--agent`: override model or agent profile.
- `--qwen-router`: experimental optimized Qwen router.
- `--yolo`: deprecated alias for `--skip-approvals`; does not enable AUTO.
- `--version`, `-h/--help`.

The source validates prompt-dependent combinations before loading config, database, providers, or MCP. Empty prompts, `--tools`, `--json`, and identity flags without `--prompt` are rejected. `--mode`, `--auto`, and `--plan` conflicts are rejected by mode parsing. Tests in `cmd/local-agent/*_test.go` preserve exact errors and exit codes.

Interactive slash commands are registered by the completion/command surface in `internal/ui` and exercised in command/completion tests. The source-visible commands include `/help`, `/theme`, `/mouse`, `/provider`, `/model`, `/settings`, `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/new`, `/clear`, `/mode`, `/plan`, `/goal`, `/commit`, `/context`, `/resume`, `/export`, `/doctor`, `/mcp`, `/skill`, `/tools`, and `/quit`/`/exit`; several have subcommands or picker forms. Exact command routing belongs to `internal/command` and the UI completion registry, rather than to the model renderer.

## Input and keybindings

`internal/ui/keys.go` is the authoritative key map. Important defaults:

- Enter sends or queues one follow-up; Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, and Alt+Enter insert a newline.
- Esc cancels/ closes the active surface; Ctrl+C quits.
- Ctrl+L clears the view; Ctrl+N starts a new conversation; F1/Ctrl+H opens help.
- Alt+T toggles all tool receipts; Ctrl+T toggles the focused/last tool.
- PgUp/PgDn page the transcript; Ctrl+U/Ctrl+D half-page when the composer is empty; End jumps latest.
- Tab/Ctrl+I opens/selects completion; Up/Down navigate completion or input history.
- Ctrl+Y copies selection or the last assistant response; Ctrl+V pastes text/image.
- Alt+O/Alt+D inspect full tool output/diff; Alt+M toggles mouse capture; Alt+R toggles reasoning; Alt+C toggles compact receipt mode.
- Shift+Tab cycles NORMAL → PLAN → AUTO; Ctrl+O opens model picker; Ctrl+P settings; Ctrl+G agents; Ctrl+F transcript search; Ctrl+E external editor.

Ownership is state-dependent. `handleIdleKey`, `handleBusyOperationKey`, and `handleOverlayKey` ensure an overlay or host operation owns all input, a focused non-empty composer keeps printable keys, and transcript paging never falls through to the textarea. Approval uses Esc, Enter, `n`, `y`, with additional scoped choices (`s`, `a`, `p`, `w`, `m`, `e`) and detail/scroll controls (`d`, PgUp/PgDn) in `internal/ui/approval.go`.

## TUI composition and state ownership

The root Bubble Tea `ui.Model` in `internal/ui/model.go` owns state and routes messages. It contains the Bubbles textarea, viewport, spinner, transcript entries, streaming buffers, overlays, approval state, model/provider pickers, session/goal state, tool receipt viewers, completion/search state, geometry/cache state, theme and mouse state. Child components expose state/update/render behavior; the parent decides which surface owns a message.

The transcript is a semantic entry list rendered through `internal/ui/messages.go`, `markdown.go`, `frame_projection.go`, and content-grid/geometry helpers. Tool receipts, diffs, outputs, reasoning, system notices, and assistant prose have distinct projections. The viewport uses an anchor/follow model so streaming updates do not jump a user who scrolled up. `content_grid.go` reserves the accent/chrome column and `geometry.go` computes responsive widths/heights. Minimum-width tests cover narrow terminals and preserve footer/composer usability.

Overlays include help, model/provider selection, settings, agents, sessions, theme, mode, cloud consent, context doctor, runtime status, goal forms/recovery/inspector, transcript search, completion, output, and diff viewers. `internal/ui/agenthub.go` supplies agent activity/list/detail views. `internal/ui/approval.go` owns approval choices and confirmation for broader/durable scopes. `internal/ui/composer_chrome.go` and `composer_flow.go` own draft height, mode presentation, completion, history, paste, and follow-up queue behavior.

The three authority modes are in `internal/ui/mode.go`: NORMAL allows interactive tools with approval, PLAN is read/explore-only, and AUTO is proactive with configured scoped authority. A linked goal runtime presents AUTO regardless of the ambient mode selector. Modes also select preferred model capability and router mode. These are authority contracts, not merely colors or labels.

## Themes and rendering

`internal/ui/theme.go` defines the semantic palette and built-in schemes: nord, catppuccin, dracula, everforest, gruvbox, kanagawa, one, rose-pine, solarized, and tokyo-night. Theme roles are explicit and contrast-tested; `/theme` previews and persists the selected scheme in runtime preferences. UI config `ui.theme` is presentation-only and unknown schemes fall back safely. `ui.prose_width` defaults to following terminal width (`0`), with bounds 40–500 when pinned. Markdown, code fences, diffs, tables, inspectors, status, approval, and tool receipts use different semantic rendering paths.

## Configuration defaults and provider admission

`config.example.yaml` documents local Ollama as default: `ollama.base_url` `http://localhost:11434`, model `qwen3.5:2b`, and `num_ctx` 16384. Profiles support `ollama`, `ollama_remote`, `openai_compatible`, and `xai`. XAI defaults to `https://api.x.ai/v1`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `grok-4.5`, and context 131072. OpenAI-compatible defaults context 128000. Credentials are environment-variable names only; TinyVault injection is recommended.

`privacy.local_only: true` rejects remote Ollama and remote MCP endpoints. `sandbox.enabled` is false by default; `allow_network` is false. Tool defaults include 30s command timeout, max grep results 500, max iterations 10, AUTO segment max 40, and whole-turn AUTO defaults of 8 segments/90m when omitted. Approval timeout is optional and indefinite by default; the UI warns that unattended AUTO can park forever without one. Continuations default `suggest` with max two automatic steps. ICE is enabled by default, uses local Ollama embeddings (`nomic-embed-text`), and stores managed state under the user config directory.

`internal/llm` implements Ollama, remote Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, and XAI adapters. `manager.go` handles model lifecycle/switching; `model_admission.go` validates model inventory, context sizing, memory/weight limits, and local/cloud routing before prompt data is sent. Remote profiles require local-only privacy opt-out. Tests cover remote routing, API-key environment names, inventory, admission, retries, reasoning settings, and provider switches.

## Chalupa/remote profiles

The historical source refers to remote Ollama profiles and SSH-forward/Chalupa-style endpoints as explicit provider profiles. The profile supplies base URL, model, context size, optional API-key env name, model-byte ceiling, and stream-idle timeout. The host consumes the process-scoped profile; it does not infer GPU ownership from a loopback URL. Remote/cloud selection is separated from model admission and local-only policy.

## MCP

`internal/mcp` separates registry/configuration, executable policy, stdio lifecycle, HTTP policy, environment allowlists, health status, tracing, and client calls. `config.example.yaml` treats MCP as a separate tool boundary from built-in tools. `internal/config/default_mcp_trust.yaml` and trust tests define catalog/trust behavior. HTTP policy checks local-only rules and redirects; stdio uses bounded subprocess lifecycle, explicit environment construction, stderr/lifecycle handling, and process-group cleanup. Registry tests cover duplicate names, status/health, trust, pagination/size contracts, transport errors, and lifecycle. `internal/ecosystem` consumes bounded MCP projections and receipt documents: transport success is not domain success or evidence, and raw structured output is not concatenated into transcript/session text.

Actual historical behavior is the adapter/registry and UI approval integration present in source/tests. Any future MCP gateway or automatic tool proxy described in comments is planned unless a corresponding call path and test exists.

## Skills and instruction loading

`internal/skill` manages workspace/user skill discovery, metadata/types, activation, and tests. Skills are separate from model/provider configuration and are loaded as instruction context under bounded validation. `internal/config/default_agentignore` and config path code control ignored files and startup discovery. `internal/agent` composes host instructions, project `AGENTS.md` instructions, tool policy, mode authority, scoped permissions, approvals, checkpoints, and continuation rules. `internal/initcmd` creates an `AGENTS.md` starter file. Instruction loading is treated as policy input; it does not grant tool authority by itself.

## Sessions, ICE, and receipts

The Go host persists sessions, execution ledgers, goals, approvals, recovery hazards, and receipts in internal DB/store packages. `/session` lists/exports/repairs saved sessions; `--resume` restores one. ICE (`internal/ice`) provides bounded local retrieval/embedding memory, with migration/store tests and workspace scoping. `internal/ecosystem` receipt projections preserve transport/domain/evidence distinctions and redact or bound raw outputs.

## Verification boundary

The commit contains extensive Go tests across command parsing, UI rendering/key ownership, provider admission, MCP lifecycle/policy, session/recovery, ICE, skills, and ecosystem contracts. Snapshot/glyph fixtures under `specs` and `internal/ui` are presentation contracts. The experimental TypeScript client in the current workspace is a separate implementation; this document records the Go interface needed before removal and does not claim feature parity.

## Exact registered slash commands

The authoritative list is `internal/command/commands.go:RegisterBuiltins` plus action registries in `actions.go`. These are the registered command names and aliases at the reference commit; names not in this list should not be recreated as historical built-ins.

| Command and aliases | Syntax / actual behavior |
|---|---|
| `/help`, `/h`, `/?` | Opens the help overlay. No arguments. |
| `/clear`, `/new` | Clears conversation history and starts a clean transcript. |
| `/plan` | Opens the guided read-only planning form; optional free-form task suffix. |
| `/goal`, `/g` | Opens goal form, shows current goal, or handles `new`, `show`, `pause`, `resume`, `budget`, `drop`; free-form objective is accepted as a new goal request. |
| `/model`, `/m`, `/models`, `/ml` | Opens model picker; `list/ls` prints inventory; `auto` enables routing; a model name switches after admission. |
| `/mouse`, `/select` | Toggles terminal mouse capture. |
| `/theme`, `/themes`, `/colors` | Opens theme picker; `list/ls` lists registered schemes; a name switches/persists the theme. |
| `/provider`, `/providers`, `/prov` | Opens provider picker; `list/ls` lists configured profiles; a profile switches after admission. |
| `/recover` | Opens recovery for an interrupted/uncertain operation when one is available. |
| `/agent`, `/a` | Opens the agent-profile picker/selection flow. |
| `/agents` | Opens the agent hub/activity surface. |
| `/load`, `/l` | Loads an agent profile or shared agent configuration according to the active context. |
| `/image`, `/attach` | Starts image attachment/paste review; image support is terminal/platform dependent. |
| `/scope` | Opens read/write scope review and temporary scope controls. |
| `/permissions`, `/perms` | Opens the permissions panel for scoped approvals and policy state. |
| `/unload` | Releases the current model/runtime selection where supported. |
| `/skill`, `/sk` | Lists/selects/activates discovered skills; applicability and activation are validated by the skill manager. |
| `/servers` | Shows configured MCP servers/status. |
| `/mcp` | Opens MCP server/tool status and inspection. It does not itself grant tool authority. |
| `/tools` | Shows or toggles native tool visibility/policy presentation. MCP tools remain a separate catalog. |
| `/ice` | Opens ICE/context memory controls. |
| `/memory`, `/mem`, `/memories` | Opens memory/ICE inspection or retrieval controls. |
| `/sessions`, `/ss`, `/resume` | Lists saved sessions and opens the session picker; `/resume` is an alias. |
| `/artifacts`, `/artifact` | Opens artifact/receipt inspection. |
| `/changes` | Shows accumulated workspace changes/diffs where available. |
| `/commit`, `/ci` | Starts the commit review/approval workflow; it owns a cancellable local-model plus Git transaction. |
| `/context`, `/numctx`, `/ctx` | Shows context-window/model context information. |
| `/stats` | Shows usage/runtime statistics. |
| `/export` | Exports a session/transcript/receipt through the atomic filesystem workflow. |
| `/import` | Imports bounded context/session material with validation. |
| `/checkpoint`, `/cp` | Creates or inspects a durable checkpoint. |
| `/checkpoints` | Lists checkpoint state. |
| `/restore` | Restores a checkpoint/recovery state. |
| `/exit`, `/quit`, `/q` | Requests application shutdown. |

Command matching is registry-based and supports completion. Custom commands are loaded separately by `internal/command/custom.go`; they cannot override a built-in or earlier custom command. Tests in `commands_test.go`, `custom_test.go`, and `complete_test.go` are the source of truth for parsing and completion behavior. A command that appears only in old prose or an abandoned migration test is not part of this registered list.

## Configuration file search and precedence

`internal/config` loads a bounded YAML document (startup limit 1 MiB) from repository/XDG/user locations. The documented order is repository `./local-agent.yaml`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/local-agent/config.yaml`, then `$HOME/.config/local-agent/config.yaml`; the selected source path is runtime metadata and is not serialized. Environment overrides include `LOCAL_AGENT_PROVIDER` for active provider selection and the documented local-only/provider environment switches. Configuration tests in `config_*_test.go` cover path precedence, symlink/regular-file checks, startup timeouts, and migration errors.

Top-level nested settings are `ollama`, `provider`, `model`, `agents`, `servers`, `ice`, `agent_profile`, `tools`, `continuations`, `experts`, `privacy`, `sandbox`, and `ui`. `skills_dir` is retained only to reject a retired split skill root with a migration error. Explicit null continuation configuration is rejected; omission means safe defaults.

The local Ollama defaults in the example are base URL `http://localhost:11434`, model `qwen3.5:2b`, context allocation `16384`, and optional `disable_reasoning`. Provider profiles may define `type`, `base_url`, `model`, `api_key_env`, `context_size`, `max_model_bytes`, and `stream_idle_timeout`. Secrets are never YAML values; `api_key_env` names a process environment variable. The profile catalog uses `provider.active` plus `provider.profiles`; the flat provider form remains accepted. An absent provider block resolves to local Ollama.

`model.models` entries carry name/family/size/parameters/context/capability/default/exclusive metadata. The example auto-router defaults to `qwen3.5:2b`, fallback chain `qwen3.5:2b`, `qwen3.5:0.8b`, `qwen3.5:4b`, and local embedding model `nomic-embed-text`. Exclusive models are manual selections and are not automatic candidates. Model admission verifies inventory, capability, context allocation, and memory/weight ceilings before inference.

`tools` defaults are command timeout 30s, grep result cap 500, interactive max iterations 10, and configurable AUTO segment/whole-turn ceilings. `builtin_tools` omitted means mode defaults; an explicit empty list disables native tools. `continuations.mode` defaults `suggest`, with `max_auto_steps` default two. `experts.enabled` defaults true, zero concurrency values mean measured automatic limits, and evaluation output is bounded by `max_eval_tokens` (example 768) with a 90s timeout.

`privacy.local_only` defaults true. `sandbox.enabled` defaults false and `sandbox.allow_network` defaults false. `ui.theme` accepts the registered ten-ish built-in schemes and is presentation-only. `ui.prose_width` zero follows terminal width; explicit bounds are 40–500. `ice.enabled` defaults true; an empty ICE path uses managed user configuration storage, while relative configured paths are rooted beneath the managed ICE directory and absolute paths/`..` escapes are rejected.

## MCP discovery and lifecycle details

`internal/mcp/registry.go` owns a lifecycle context, close-once state, connection epoch, connection-attempt generation, server config catalog, exposed tool route map, failed-server records, health monitor wait group, and dirty/list-changed refresh workers. A connection operation is admitted under a lifecycle lock; `Registry.Close` cancels the lifecycle context and waits for admitted operations so a child process cannot outlive shutdown.

`discoverServer` is the production connector. It calls the version/trust/tool-change handshake, lists tools with the connection context, closes the client if listing fails, converts each bounded MCP tool to an LLM tool definition, and only then publishes the route/catalog. Initial list-change notifications are suppressed until the authoritative first list completes; later notifications schedule a refresh. Reconnect attempts are generation checked so stale attempts cannot replace newer connections. Failed servers retain name/reason status rather than masquerading as an empty successful catalog.

Connection timeout is 15 seconds; default individual MCP call timeout is 60 seconds and can be overridden on the registry. Health status tracks connected, last error, and last ping. HTTP policy enforces local-only mode, allowed origin/host and redirect behavior. Stdio policy validates executable/configuration, builds an explicit environment, bounds executable size, and closes process groups. Registry/tool tests cover startup failure, cancellation, close overlap, stale epochs, tool-list refresh, duplicate names, pagination/oversized pages, and health status.

The ecosystem projection in `internal/ecosystem` handles supported contracts and versions, including MCPHub assembly, shared envelopes, receipt documents, verifier projections, and bounded contract fixtures. Transport success, domain success, and evidence are separate states. `isError: false` from a transport is not proof that a domain operation succeeded; raw `StructuredContent` remains at the adapter/parser boundary and is never concatenated into model transcript text or persisted UI/session state. Supported contract fixtures include MCPHub complete/invalid/oversized pages, stored envelopes, call-ID mismatch, Cortex shared-envelope success/rejection, and unknown structured output.

## Skills, instruction loading, and applicability

`internal/skill.Manager` searches explicit skill directories only; an empty directory disables discovery. It accepts ordinary `.md` files or directories containing `SKILL.md`/`skill.md`, skips dotfiles, rejects symlinks, bounds each file and catalog, parses frontmatter, validates UTF-8/name/description, rejects duplicate names, and sorts deterministically. Skill names are capped at 128 bytes, descriptions at 512 bytes, catalog entries at 64, and catalog bytes at 32 KiB. The manager preserves active status across reloads.

The manager does not infer applicability from a filename or grant authority. Activation/selection is an instruction-context choice and remains subject to mode/tool policy, approvals, workspace boundaries, and host authority. `AGENTS.md` project instructions are loaded separately from skill discovery. `init` creates an `AGENTS.md` starter. Host instructions, project instructions, selected skill content, provider/model policy, and mode prefix are composed before the agent turn; none of these text sources independently authorizes shell, mutation, secrets, MCP, or network access.

## Provider/model vision, reasoning, embeddings, and budgets

The provider abstraction keeps transport, admission, and authority distinct. Ollama is the default local transport. Remote Ollama is a configured profile, not inferred from an arbitrary loopback URL. OpenAI-compatible and XAI profiles use named environment credentials and explicit remote privacy opt-out. `internal/llm/manager.go` unloads/switches models and reconciles inventory; `remote_ollama.go`, `openai_compatible.go`, and `ollama.go` implement provider-specific streaming/cancellation behavior.

Model admission checks exact available inventory and configured limits before sending conversation data. Context size is an allocation request, not a promise of model maximum; the example warns that 262144 on a 16GB machine can force swap/OOM. Exclusive/deep models are manual. Capability routing maps SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX/ADVANCED work to the configured candidate set and avoids exclusive models for automatic routing.

Reasoning is a provider/model feature. Ollama can disable reasoning for templates that support `think=false`; the UI keeps reasoning rows inspectable and offers Alt+R to toggle all completed reasoning receipts. Reasoning is not silently treated as assistant answer text. Streaming idle timeouts default to five minutes for provider paths unless configured; cancellation remains immediate. Tests cover reasoning config, idle timeout, retries, remote handoff, and stream closure.

Experts are read-only, tool-free consultations, not token-level mixture-of-experts. Team/Swarm/MoE modes fan out bounded local inference subject to measured CPU/RAM and configured concurrency caps. Their outputs are advisory context and do not grant tools or mutate workspace. ICE computes local embeddings through Ollama's embedding model and stores bounded workspace-scoped retrieval state; it does not send embeddings to a remote provider under local-only mode.

AUTO budgets are layered: per-segment iterations, segment count, whole-turn wall time, and approval wait timeout. Hitting a segment ceiling checkpoints and continues another bounded segment; repeating work without verified effects triggers a stall guard. Approval timeout withholds permission and records refusal; it never grants an unattended tool. PLAN disallows writes even when an approval callback could otherwise allow them; NORMAL is interactive; AUTO has scoped proactive authority with explicit pauses for Git, destructive/dynamic shell, secrets, network endpoints, unknown commands, and genuine human decisions.

## Rebuild acceptance checklist

A replacement must preserve the exact root flags/exit behavior, registered slash-command names and aliases, mode authority boundaries, multiline composer semantics, transcript anchor/scroll behavior, approval choices and cancellation, model admission/privacy policy, provider credential handling, MCP lifecycle cleanup and evidence projections, skill bounds/applicability separation, session/recovery/ICE boundaries, and receipt distinction between transport, domain, and evidence. The Go tests and glyph/snapshot fixtures at the reference commit are compatibility evidence; comments describing future tools, gateways, or migrations are not proof of released behavior.

## Detailed surface ownership map

The main update path is deliberately ordered by ownership rather than widget order. Startup/session/provider/model loading owns input until a tokened result returns. A running foreground turn owns cancellation and follow-up queue behavior. Approval owns every key while visible. An overlay owns every key while open, including unknown keys, so printable input cannot leak into the composer underneath it.

The composer is a Bubbles textarea with dynamic row height. It stores the draft separately from transcript entries, inserts literal newlines through the newline bindings, tracks completion suppression after Escape, supports history navigation only on an empty/active-history draft, and can hand a draft to `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR`. A non-empty draft intentionally blocks global printable shortcuts and most modal-opening chords. A visible queued follow-up receives the first Escape; a later Escape cancels the active turn.

The transcript parent owns document scroll and follows the latest output until the user pages upward. Streaming paints update a live tail without rebuilding every stable receipt. Reflow anchors use semantic entry/block identity and line offsets rather than raw viewport coordinates. Collapsed read runs, tool cards, thinking rows, diffs, and output inspectors each have stable semantic targets. A no-tool turn clears stale receipt inspection so Alt+O/Alt+D cannot point at an earlier turn.

Responsive layout starts from a content grid with a reserved accent/chrome column. The right rail/sidebar and footer compete for terminal rows/columns through geometry helpers; narrow terminals hide or reduce secondary surfaces rather than allowing the composer or approval footer to overlap the transcript. Minimum terminal tests cover widths/heights where the help, approval, picker, and inline form surfaces must remain usable.

Mouse capture is on by default so wheel scrolling and in-app drag selection work. Alt+M or `/mouse` hands mouse selection to the terminal emulator and clears the in-app selection. Ctrl+Y copies the current selection or the last assistant answer only when the composer is empty. Clipboard image paste enters an explicit review/attachment flow and is bounded; it does not silently become a prompt or an external file.

Model/provider pickers are overlays with filtered lists, model details, inventory refresh, pull, cloud consent, and admission reasons. A picker selection commits only on Enter; Escape closes/reverts. Provider switching cancels or serializes runtime admission and inventory refresh. The current provider/model is shown in status chrome but the status line does not imply successful domain work.

Settings owns presentation and operational preferences separately. Theme preview changes the frame immediately but persists only on Enter; Escape restores the committed theme. Mode picker changes ambient mode and router preference, while a linked durable goal owns presented AUTO authority. The settings surface does not turn a visual selection into an approval or execution grant.

Agent hub is an inspectable activity/consultation surface. It can be opened while a foreground turn streams when the draft is empty, but it does not steal a non-empty draft. Its viewer uses stable agent/run identifiers, jump/scroll controls, and bounded projections. Expert consultation remains read-only and is never serialized as a user prompt or treated as a tool receipt.

Session picker/listing/loading has a token/generation boundary. Escape cancels a load or clears a list filter before closing. A late filesystem/database result is ignored if its generation no longer matches. Session restore replaces the complete durable transcript/runtime state; it is not a best-effort append. Recovery surfaces distinguish interrupted effects, uncertain outcomes, failed checkpoints, and ordinary cancellation.

Goal forms and inspectors are separate from ordinary prompts. `/goal` can create/show/pause/resume/budget/drop durable work; a goal runtime presents AUTO authority and reports active goal state. Goal operations own input while creating, reconciling, or recovering. `/commit` is another owned operation: it serializes composer input around local model/git review, supports Escape cancellation, and exposes actual receipts rather than assuming a successful transport means a committed change.

## Tests and compatibility evidence

The reference commit tests the command registry, aliases, custom command collision rules, completion routing, root flag combinations, provider profile normalization, model selection/admission, remote privacy, stream cancellation, MCP trust/lifecycle/health, skill parsing/bounds, ICE store/migration, session restore/recovery, approval choices, keyboard ownership, geometry, theme contrast, markdown/diff rendering, scroll anchoring, and glyph snapshots. These tests are behavior evidence for a rebuild and should be ported at the contract level rather than copied as implementation-shaped tests.

UI tests use Bubble Tea test messages (`KeyPressMsg`, paste, resize, mouse) and inspect both state transitions and rendered output. Approval tests cover deny, allow-once, broader session/path/tool scopes, two-step confirmation, Escape cancellation, viewport detail, and minimum terminal layout. Completion tests cover commands, attachments, arguments, folders, selection, dismissal, and draft restoration. Model/provider tests cover unavailable, exclusive, wrong-context, cloud consent, and router selection states.

MCP tests include deterministic contract fixtures for success/failure transport, malformed and future schema, oversized pages, call-ID mismatch, stored receipts, shared-envelope success/rejection, and unknown structured output. The important invariant is that a test may prove parsing or transport without proving the remote/domain action. Receipts must retain that distinction in serialized state and UI copy.

Configuration tests verify repository/XDG/home precedence, bounded reads, symlink rejection, invalid YAML/null subsections, default propagation, provider profile aliases, API-key environment names, local-only behavior, MCP trust and timeout, ICE path safety, and agent/skill discovery. Tests intentionally include empty explicit lists because omission means defaults while `[]` means disable.

## Historical versus replacement boundary

The Go implementation at this commit was the released-product surface. The current TypeScript client in this workspace is experimental and should not be described as having parity until each contract above is verified. In particular, a TypeScript component or MCP adapter that compiles is not evidence of equivalent Go command routing, approval scope semantics, session durability, model admission, or ecosystem receipt projections.

When removing the Go source, preserve this document and the exact reference commit so future changes can distinguish compatibility requirements from obsolete implementation details. Delete a feature only after deciding whether its user-visible contract is intentionally retired, ported, or replaced with a narrower documented behavior. Do not infer that a name in a comment, a stale snapshot, or an unused type was reachable from the CLI.

## Configuration field reference

| Section | Fields/defaults | Authority or presentation meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama` | `model: qwen3.5:2b`, `base_url: http://localhost:11434`, `num_ctx: 16384`, optional `disable_reasoning` | Local transport and KV-cache allocation; `num_ctx` is a request allocation, not model maximum. |
| `provider` | flat `type/base_url/model/api_key_env/context_size/max_model_bytes/stream_idle_timeout`; catalog `active/profiles` | Selects one inference adapter; env names identify secrets but values stay process-owned. |
| `model` | model descriptors, default, fallback chain, `auto_select`, `embed_model` | Routing/admission catalog; exclusive entries require explicit selection. |
| `agents` | `dir`, `auto_load` | Shared agent profile discovery; loaded instructions do not grant tools. |
| `servers` | MCP server name, transport/command/args/env/url/trust fields | External tool catalog and trust boundary; separate from native tools. |
| `tools` | `builtin_tools`, `timeout`, `max_grep_results`, iteration/AUTO ceilings, `approval_timeout` | Native tool policy and bounded execution budgets. |
| `continuations` | `mode: suggest`, `max_auto_steps: 2` | Typed follow-up suggestions; automatic mode is limited and read-only contracts are exact. |
| `experts` | enabled, concurrency caps, eval token cap, timeout | Read-only local consultation budget. |
| `privacy` | `local_only: true` | Rejects remote Ollama/MCP unless explicitly opted out. |
| `sandbox` | `enabled: false`, `allow_network: false` | OS-level child-process confinement; second layer below catalog authority. |
| `ui` | theme, prose width 0/follow-terminal | Presentation only; never changes tool authority. |
| `ice` | enabled, managed/relative `store_path`, embedding settings | Workspace-scoped local retrieval/memory; path escapes rejected. |
| `agent_profile` | selected profile name | Chooses shared agent instructions/configuration. |

Profile resolution precedence is: explicit CLI `--model`/`--agent`, process provider override, saved provider preference when no process override, config `provider.active`, an explicit `ollama` catalog profile, then the first sorted profile; absent provider config resolves to local Ollama. Interactive `/provider` changes the active profile and persists the manual provider preference separately from the YAML catalog. Model picker selections are subject to inventory/admission and may trigger an unload/switch before the new model becomes current.

## Ecosystem projection and supported contract families

The ecosystem package is a bounded projection layer, not a generic JSON gateway. It has dedicated receipt/projection paths for Bob guidance/artifacts, Cortex decisions/shared envelopes, Hitspec, Filecheap, Codemap, Vecgrep, Vidtrace, monitor receipts, and MCPHub assembly. Each adapter validates a versioned fixture/contract, records transport/domain/evidence state independently, and stores only bounded fields needed for UI/session continuity.

MCPHub assembly has explicit complete-page, invalid-page, oversized-page, stored-result, and call-ID mismatch fixtures. A missing page cursor, malformed envelope, future schema version, mismatched call identity, or over-limit output is a bounded failure, not an empty success. Unknown structured output is retained inside the parser boundary for diagnostics but is excluded from transcript text and durable UI state.

Bob guidance separates context-clean, conflict, drift, managed-path, extension, missing-input, and ready projections. Cortex shared envelopes distinguish gate rejection from accepted evidence. Failure fixtures distinguish transport failure from domain failure. Receipt documents include verifier projections and artifact references; a successful process exit or MCP response alone never becomes “verified.”

The historical UI surfaces ecosystem status, receipts, and recovery through dedicated cards/viewers. Those surfaces may show “transport succeeded,” “domain result unavailable,” or “evidence unverified” simultaneously. Rebuilds must preserve these labels instead of collapsing them into a generic success/error boolean.

## Skill discovery reference

The canonical shared skills root is selected by the application/config layer; the manager receives an explicit search directory and does not recursively search arbitrary workspace paths. A skill is either `name.md` at the directory root or a named directory containing `SKILL.md`/`skill.md`. Hidden entries and package-manager links are skipped/rejected deliberately. Symlinked skill directories/files are rejected to avoid an unreviewed path crossing.

Frontmatter can declare name/description and optional applicability metadata. Missing name falls back to the filename/directory name. Names reject control/format characters and whitespace errors; descriptions and bodies are bounded. Duplicate names across search paths fail loading rather than silently choosing one. Catalog order is deterministic by name/path, and reload preserves each existing skill's active flag.

Applicability is a selection/context concern: a skill may be offered by completion or `/skill`, but activation must match the current workspace/task and remains subordinate to AGENTS/project instructions, mode policy, host approvals, and tool catalogs. A skill cannot authorize a network request, shell command, file mutation, secret read, or MCP call merely by containing instructions that request it.

## Provider transport and admission flow

Startup loads configuration, resolves the provider profile, builds the model router, opens model inventory/admission state, and only then starts the UI/agent loop. The process may print warnings for unavailable saved preferences or inventory; it must not claim a model is usable until admission returns a validated model projection. Remote provider API keys are read from the named environment variable at the adapter boundary, never persisted in config/session/transcript.

A streaming turn sends a bounded Message history and tool definitions to the selected provider. The transport validates stream chunks, enforces idle/header timeouts, supports immediate cancellation, and closes its client stream in `finally`. The agent layer owns tool authority and approval; the LLM adapter only transports model messages/events. Tool arguments are schema-bounded before host execution, and receipts contain actual output/status rather than inferred success.

Reasoning tokens/events are separate from assistant content. The UI can collapse or expand completed reasoning, while a mode/provider setting can disable reasoning for compatible Ollama templates. Embeddings use the configured local embedding model for ICE and do not become conversation content. Expert calls are tool-free and read-only, with explicit token/time/concurrency budgets.

## Removal readiness

Before Go deletion, archive this reference with the source commit and retain the Go test/snapshot artifacts needed to interpret future compatibility failures. Verify the TypeScript CLI has an intentional answer for every listed root flag, slash command, approval scope, session/recovery path, provider policy, MCP projection, skill bound, and ecosystem receipt state. Where parity is intentionally absent, record the retirement or replacement decision next to the new interface rather than silently dropping the behavior.

# Historical Go Runtime Reference

Reference commit: 2567a7a7468ef2a1591e289f43d62b78b5c9679a. This document is a reconstruction guide for the released Go runtime. Paths and symbols refer to that commit. It distinguishes wired behavior from package contracts and tests.

## Agent loop and authority

internal/agent/agent.go owns mutable conversation history, model/router configuration, workspace policy, memory, MCP registry, ICE, continuation settings, tool availability, and session approval grants. New, AddUserMessage, Messages, ReplaceMessagesWithinSession, RestoreMessagesWithinSession, SetWorkDir, SetPermissionChecker, SetExecutionLedger, and Close are the main host surface. ContextPromptFloor and its record/restore methods preserve a minimum prompt budget after compaction.

The turn pipeline is split across loop.go, loop_stages.go, loop_provider.go, loop_dispatch.go, loop_authorize.go, loop_errors.go, and loop_budget.go. Provider output becomes assistant text/thinking/tool calls; each call is preflighted, canonically hashed, admitted, authorized, durably recorded, dispatched, and rendered as a bounded tool result. Cancellation closes undispatched calls and cancels tracked calls. Provider errors are classified by explicit retry policy. Iteration, context, wall-time, continuation, approval, and recovery limits stop the loop.

execution.go wires ExecutionLedger, SetExecutionSessionID, SetExecutionRunID, SetExecutionSnapshotCursor, RecheckExecutionRecovery, and RequireExecutionLedger. UnresolvedExecutionError carries identity/tool/cause and RecoveryInspectCommand. Recovery cannot be rechecked while a turn is running. db/execution_events.go is append-only lifecycle storage; db/execution_hazards.go supplies effective recovery projections.

internal/tools/definitions.go exposes grep, read, write, glob, bash, bash_output, ls, find, diff, edit, mkdir, remove, copy, move, exists, load_skill, consult_experts, and ask_user. agent/tools.go filters by active policy and dispatches. Unknown tools fail.

permission/checker.go defines ask/allow/deny/yolo policies, exact ApprovalRequest/ApprovalResponse records, previews, and session scope kinds. NewChecker, Check, SetPolicy, Reset, and ResolveApprovalContext are the public operations. Broad tool allows fail with ErrBroadAllowUnsupported. approval.go creates immutable argument snapshots/hashes, workspace scope, previews and consequences, then revalidates immediately before dispatch. Session grants are exact-tool, path, bash-prefix, MCP-tool, or MCP-server scopes through approvalGrantKey, sessionToolGrantKey, sessionPathGrantKey, sessionBashPrefixGrantKey, sessionMCPToolGrantKey, and sessionMCPServerGrantKey. Workspace rules are loaded through ReloadWorkspaceRules and WorkspaceRulesStore. Tests: approval_contract_test.go, approval_metadata_test.go, approval_persistence_test.go, approval_timeout_test.go, authority_workspace_pin_test.go, scope_authority_test.go, destructive_test.go, and workspace_rules_test.go.

## Tool schemas, behavior, and errors

tools_read.go:
- handleRead accepts path plus optional offset/limit. It requires a path, resolves only workspace-readable roots, rejects escapes/ignored paths/directories/invalid reads, reports missing files and offset beyond length, and bounds output.
- handleGrep accepts pattern/path/include/context. It validates regex and include globs, walks permitted roots, checks cancellation, bounds results, and reports invalid pattern/path/walk/cancel errors.
- handleGlob accepts a bounded pattern/root, rejects invalid patterns and inaccessible/escaped roots, checks cancellation, and returns only permitted matches.
Tests are read_roots_test.go, search_coverage_test.go, and tools_test.go.

tools_write.go:
- handleWrite accepts path/content; it creates approved parents and uses pinned safe I/O, regular-file checks, UTF-8/size limits, existing identity, and atomic publication.
- handleEdit accepts either old_string/new_string or patch, never both. Replacement requires nonempty old_string, rejects no-op and ambiguous matches, supports explicit replace_all, gives near-miss guidance, and preserves literal replacement text. Patch mode is bounded and exact.
- handleMkdir creates permitted directories.
- handleRemove refuses workspace-root removal and unsafe/symlink/excluded paths.
- handleCopy and handleMove require source/destination, regular safe files, permitted parents, and reject unsupported directory copying/root moves.
Errors are returned as bounded error text plus failed status. Tests: tools_write_test.go, edit_diff_test.go, argument_privacy_test.go.

tools_diff.go handleDiff accepts path/new_content, reads a bounded existing file, computes cancellation-aware contextual LCS diff, rejects oversized matrices and missing inputs, and returns a diff or explicit cancellation/size error.

tools_bash.go handleBash accepts command and timeout/background controls. It clamps timeout to the advertised range, sanitizes environment, resolves executable/sandbox policy, captures stdout/stderr through capped buffers, applies platform confinement, and distinguishes confinement failure, cancellation, timeout, and command failure. bash_output reads owned background output. Tests include tools_bash_timeout_test.go, process-group, output-cap, and cancellation tests.

tools_fs.go implements mkdir/remove/copy/move with workspace-root and safe destination guards. tools_ask_user.go accepts question, kind (single/multiple/freeform), and bounded unique options; it requires a callback, validates option IDs/labels/counts, honors context cancellation, and formats selected answers. skills.go loads approved skill content. experts.go/consult_experts returns bounded non-authoritative consultation. Tests cover limits, provenance and cancellation.

MCP is namespaced and policy gated. SetMCPServerScope, DenyAllMCPTools, ReconnectMCPServer, MCPToolSummaries and mcp_guidance.go expose only configured server__tool names. Server instructions are untrusted guidance and cannot override system/user/project/workspace policy. mcp_preflight_test.go, mcp_guidance_test.go and mcphub_assembly_test.go cover namespacing, scope, typed status and parser boundaries.

## Input/output and privacy

argument_privacy.go redacts sensitive keys and bounds nested values before logs or previews. output.go, headless_output.go, json_output.go, and semantic_output.go separate tool start/result, user text, semantic status and transport events. Successful transport is never domain success. mcp_status.go preserves health/transport state separately from evidence. trace.go logs lifecycle metadata with a 240-byte snippet cap. maxToolCaptureBytes bounds captured tool output; capToolResultForContext adds explicit truncation/error markers. Raw MCP structured content stays at parser boundary. Relevant tests: transient_content_test.go, semantic_output_test.go, trace_test.go, json_output_test.go.

## Safe I/O, workspace and sandbox

safeio is the write authority. openWithinRoot, openNoFollow, openFollow, readRegularFileAt, publishPath, and lockPath use directory FDs, openat/no-follow flags, regular-file checks, canonical containment, and atomic temp-write/rename. publish_path.go verifies parent/file identity between approval and commit. Symlink swaps, FIFOs, devices, directories and outside-root paths fail closed. open_within_posix.go, open_nofollow_posix.go, open_follow_posix.go, regular_file.go, lock_fcntl.go and lock_flock.go implement platform backends. Tests cover races, modes, atomicity and cross-process locks.

agent/workspace_root.go, read_roots.go and sandbox.go canonicalize workspace, project instructions, .agentignore, readable leaves and additional write authority. resolveWorkspacePath and resolveDestructivePath reject lexical/symlink escapes and ignored paths.

sandbox/sandbox.go defines normalized Policy with workspace, unreadable/secret paths, readable leaves, network permission, cache roots and executable. Apply and Wrap use sandbox-exec on Darwin and bwrap/namespaces on Linux; unsupported hosts return ErrUnsupported. Secret components are denied at any depth and unexpressible policies fail closed. sandbox_test.go executes real kernel confinement and tests normalization, symlinks, network and secrets.

netpolicy/loopback.go validates loopback-only endpoints, rejects credentials/fragments/remote hosts unless explicitly allowed. execpath/resolve.go resolves executable names through controlled PATH and rejects unsafe/ambiguous paths. hostenv supplies platform allocator/environment behavior; tools_bash.go sanitizedEnv keeps only approved variables and removes provider credentials.

## Execution identity and recovery

internal/execution/types.go Identity is immutable and includes SessionID, WorkspaceID, RunID, TurnID, ExecutionID, IdempotencyKey, ProviderCallID, CanonicalCallID, ToolName, Iteration, Ordinal, Kind and EffectClass (lines 150-165). Validate requires positive IDs/iteration/ordinal, bounded UTF-8 strings, valid kind/effect and lowercase hashes. Event.Validate also bounds ResultReceipt to MaxResultReceiptBytes and Detail to MaxDetailBytes and checks UTF-8 (lines 214-259). Lifecycle is requested -> approval_requested/started/denied; approval_requested -> approved/denied; approved -> started; started -> completed/failed/cancelled/outcome_unknown. Terminal edges cannot be extended.

db/execution_events.go AppendExecutionEvent validates defaults, session/workspace scope, execution plus idempotency collisions, argument digest continuity, transition, request collisions, and exact replay. GetExecutionState/ListExecutionEvents derive raw state. LatestExecutionEventID is the snapshot cursor. ListExecutionRecoveryHazards and ListExecutionReconciliationTargets are bounded, cursor/turn-aware projections.

db/execution_hazards.go listEffectiveExecutionStates pages raw candidates, validates exact reconciliation receipts before skipping, avoids resolved rows consuming limits, fails closed on corruption/overflow, and distinguishes ordinary unresolved hazards from goal-owned reconciliation. ProjectExecutionRecovery returns bounded hazards plus only validated goal-less contexts.

db/session_recovery_state.go and reconciliation_session.go validate UTF-8/JSON, reject duplicate top-level keys and unsupported versions, enforce goal/session identity, preserve unknown envelope fields, and require nonnegative execution_cursor. outcomeUnknownTurn requires one exact blocker/reference-to-turn correlation and rejects pending turn admission.

reconciliation_groups.go EnsureReconciliationGroup snapshots all exact hazards into deterministic group/member IDs, event hashes, control-item payload hashes and a bounded member set. reconciliation_inspection.go is read-only and verifies current event IDs/types/effect classes, payload digests and completed post-cursor effects. standalone_reconciliation.go offers InspectStandaloneExecutionReconciliation and ResolveStandaloneExecutionReconciliation with immutable target tokens (session revision, event ID, execution ID, argument digest), canonical control items, typed evidence, actor and closed host context. reconciliation_commit.go atomically resolves member evidence and then the parent goal transition under lease and CAS; it rejects stale evidence, mixed/corrupt state, incomplete members, and post-cursor effectful completions. It never redispatches provider work.

Tests defining invariants include execution_crash_test.go, execution_events_test.go, execution_hazards_test.go, session_recovery_state_test.go, session_projection_repair_test.go, reconciliation_inspection_test.go, reconciliation_commit_test.go, standalone_reconciliation_test.go, turn_receipt_test.go, checkpoint_test.go and continuation*_test.go. They assert no automatic retry after uncertain effects, exact replay, cursor monotonicity, bounded context, CAS rollback, leases, append-only rows, typed receipts and transport/domain/evidence separation.

## Command and durable session UI

internal/command/registry.go, commands.go, actions.go and custom.go implement slash commands for goals, sessions/resume, provider/model switching, artifacts, permissions, approvals and recovery. Inputs are validated and return structured results. commands_test.go, actions_test.go, custom_test.go and provider_switch_test.go cover this surface.

Session state is revisioned and lossless. db/session_state.go SaveSessionStateCAS uses a transaction-local compare-and-swap and returns the committed revision. Recovery never silently retries an unknown tool. UI session restore and goal recovery consume typed inspection/receipt projections.

## Resource, image, capability and logs

resource/probe.go plus probe_linux.go/probe_darwin.go/probe_other.go collect bounded CPU/memory/GPU facts. planner.go, profile.go and types.go produce deterministic resource plans; this is advisory and never provisions infrastructure or infers GPU ownership from a loopback URL. Tests cover probes, limits and platform fallback.

imageasset/store.go validates MIME/size/digest, stores immutable assets under controlled paths, and returns references rather than arbitrary model bytes. agent/images.go resolves approved references. Tests cover digest identity, missing/corrupt assets and limits.

capabilityadvisor/advisor.go, query.go and parser.go provide a non-authoritative MCP-backed recommender. Advise validates bounded objective/phase/current/outcome/kinds/intent/catalog revision, deduplicates concurrent calls, caches only normalized validated results, expires/invalidate-on-revision, and never dispatches a recommendation. parser.go accepts exact JSON, allowlists recommendation/alternatives/required fields, rejects instruction-like/unsafe content, typed errors, inconsistent status and mismatched catalog revisions. advisor_test.go covers cache generations, expiry, cancellation, ambiguity, invalid envelopes and concurrency.

drift/drift_test.go compares duplicated/shared Go package trees and reports file-level drift; it is a guard, not runtime behavior. logging/logger.go creates mode-restricted per-session logs. logging/reader.go lists bounded recent logs, finds latest and tails lines. Tests cover modes, ordering, missing/empty directories and nil logger.

## Wired versus contract-only behavior

Wired: provider/agent loop; exact approvals and workspace rules; pinned safe I/O; OS sandbox where available; process-group commands; namespaced MCP; append-only execution ledger; CAS session state; goal and standalone reconciliation; output/logging projections; resource probes and advisor caches.

Conditional/contract-only: confinement on unsupported hosts; resource/GPU enforcement where probes are informational; advisor recommendations (never authority); MCP evidence (transport success may remain domain/evidence unknown); command execution still has user permissions under sandbox. The tests intentionally fail closed rather than upgrade unavailable evidence.

A rebuild must preserve canonical identity before dispatch, approval revalidation, no raw arguments/secrets in lifecycle rows, directory-FD writes, append-only immutable events, outcome-unknown blocking, bounded fail-closed projections, typed target-bound evidence, leases, and separate transport/domain/evidence/model-context channels.



## Exact model-visible tool schemas

The authoritative schemas are internal/tools/tools.go, not prose in the system prompt. All schemas are JSON objects; required means model-visible required, while handlers perform additional validation.

grep: required pattern string; optional path string, include glob string, context integer default 3. Handler validates regex/include and limits matches and context.
read: required path string; optional limit integer and offset integer (1-indexed). Handler rejects directories, escapes, excluded roots, invalid/oversize reads, and offset beyond EOF.
write: required path and content strings. It is whole-file replacement, parent creation is allowed, and publication is atomic.
glob: required pattern string; optional path string. Pattern is bounded and path is workspace-scoped.
bash: required command string; optional timeout integer 1..120 seconds, defaulting from host ToolTimeout, and background boolean default false. Background ignores timeout and returns an owned ID.
bash_output: optional id string; absent id lists the session's background processes. It accepts no command string and has additionalProperties false. Repeated identical reads in one turn are suppressed.
ls: optional path string, default working directory.
find: required name string; optional path string and type string f/d/both.
diff: required path and new_content strings. It is a preview and does not write.
edit: required path; either old_string/new_string or patch. Optional replace_all boolean defaults false. old_string matching is literal and exact; patch is complete unified diff with current line numbers and byte-exact context. Passing both forms is rejected.
mkdir: required path string; parent directories are created.
remove: required path; optional recursive and force booleans default false. Root removal is rejected.
copy and move: required source and destination strings; both use safe path identity checks.
exists: required path string; returns bounded existence/type information.
load_skill: required exact name string; additionalProperties false; the host resolves only the discovered catalog.
ask_user: required question string, 1..2048 chars; optional kind enum yes_no/single/freetext and options up to 8. Each option requires id 1..64 and label 1..256, optional detail up to 512. Additional properties are forbidden.
consult_experts: required strategy enum team/swarm/moe and objective 1..32768; optional experts up to 16 names (1..128), model 1..256, model_overrides up to 16 exact expert/model objects. Additional properties are forbidden. Child experts receive no tools.

Model-visible tools are narrowed by ToolPolicy in internal/agent/tool_policy.go. ASK allows read, grep, glob, ls, find, diff, exists, bash_output, load_skill, consult_experts, ask_user plus memory_recall; PLAN uses ASK and permits MCP; BUILD adds write/edit/bash/mkdir/remove/copy/move plus all memory operations and MCP. A configured kit is intersected with the mode, never expanded. NarrowedToolSystemPrompt states relative path and repetition rules.

## Mode and permission matrix

ASK is observation-only: no write/edit/remove/copy/move/bash, but bash_output can observe host-owned background work and ask_user remains available. PLAN is read/inspect/advisory: it still denies writes and command execution, but can use MCP according to explicit MCP scope; it is not a universal allow. BUILD permits effects only after exact host approval unless a matching bounded policy/session/workspace grant exists. YOLO is a policy mode, not a bypass of path/sandbox/identity validation. Memory scopes are independent from native tools.

MCP has three gates: active tool policy AllowMCP, agent MCP server/tool scope, and permission approval. A server's instructions are untrusted. Names are server__tool and bare remote names are rejected. A successful transport can produce a failed domain result or unverified evidence; it must never be converted into verified success.

Workspace policy gates every filesystem operation. .agentignore/excluded secrets are applied after canonicalization, and additional write roots are explicit. Destructive tools have separate classification in permission/destructive.go. Approval previews include exact resource, arguments hash, consequences, and scope. Revalidation catches file replacement, rule changes, changed workspace, and changed arguments before dispatch.

## Turn state, cancellation, retries and verification

At turn start the runtime captures turn ID, model, context size, authority mode, filesystem roots, tool catalog and MCP snapshot. It admits a bounded system prompt and tool schemas. If prompt pressure crosses compactThreshold (75 percent), compactForContextAndModel reserves summarizer budget, retains the newest keepMessages (4), preserves durable recovery context, and records eval tokens. If compaction fails or the prompt remains over budget, the turn stops with a context-budget error.

Provider output with no tool calls enters finishDirectResponse, which may perform optional ICE auto-memory detection, final compaction and turn logging. Tool output enters recordAssistantTurn: requested lifecycle rows are durably written before dispatch and assistant history is appended. The provider call ID, turn ID, iteration, ordinal, argument digest and canonical execution identity are retained.

For each call, preflight rejects unsupported/repeated calls, checks active policy, computes canonical argument hash, and builds approval preview. A blocked or denied call produces a tool start/result error and a terminal denial without dispatch. An authorized call records approval then started before host execution. The result is bounded and classified as success, failed, cancelled, or outcome_unknown. Cancellation after dispatch is uncertain even if the backend later returns an error; the raw execution row remains hazardous. Undispatched later calls are closed with cancelled results.

Transient provider errors are retryable only under loop_errors.go/isRetryableError and bounded retry accounting; malformed tool output is not a reason to silently repeat effects. Repeated built-ins are rejected or receive a correction, and consult_experts is limited per parent turn. Empty terminal responses arm a one-shot repair prompt; a second empty terminal is a failure. The loop has maximum iterations and explicit auto-continuation ceilings.

Verification is evidence-oriented. A command exit status is a transport/execution fact; it does not prove a product claim. MCP transport success remains domain unknown/evidence unverified. Tool results are reported with actual output, exit status, truncation and cancellation. Successful MCP or process transport cannot be rendered as verified domain success without a bounded domain receipt.

## Agent context and compaction ownership

The agent owns the conversation; UI owns presentation. checkpoint/turn receipts append user, assistant and tool messages only after the corresponding lifecycle boundary. Compaction retains durable recovery context, not raw hidden authority. compact.go preserves recent messages, summaries and typed recovery context; it fails closed when a summary cannot be validated or fit the active context. Tool results can be shrunk before hard context rejection, but execution ledger rows remain complete.

ICE indexing is optional and non-authoritative. User/assistant indexing failures are reported as optional errors; an ICE session change disables the engine. Summary indexing is similarly optional. Memory tools remain separately authorized and their returned content is bounded before model context.

## Structured data and parser boundaries

MCP raw StructuredContent is retained inside the MCP parser/control-plane boundary. mcp_guidance.go treats server instructions as untrusted quoted guidance. mcp_status.go projects transport, domain and evidence states separately. capabilityadvisor/parser.go accepts exact resolver envelopes, allowlists recommendation identity, required fields and alternatives, rejects instruction-like fields and mismatched catalog revisions, and never returns arbitrary resolver JSON as system instructions.

semantic_output.go and json_output.go separate event types for text, thinking, tool start/result, status and errors. headless output is machine-readable; terminal output is presentation. trace.go emits bounded metadata/snippets. No raw MCP structured payload, provider credential, hidden argument or unbounded tool result should enter durable session text or model context.

## Platform/resource details

sandbox/sandbox_darwin.go builds a seatbelt profile with workspace read/write rules, secret denials, temporary/cache allowances and optional network. sandbox_linux.go probes bwrap, builds bind/read-only/tmpfs/network namespace arguments, and scans secret components with a bounded entry count. sandbox_other.go reports unavailable rather than pretending confinement.

resource/probe_linux.go reads cgroup/proc facts; probe_darwin.go uses platform host facts; probe_other.go returns conservative unsupported results. planner.go converts facts and provider requirements into a bounded Plan, while profile.go validates profile names/limits. The planner is advisory; Chalupa or the provider profile owns infrastructure placement.

imageasset/store.go computes and validates content digest, extension/MIME/size, stores immutable content, and returns a reference. Agent image resolution loads only references already admitted by the host. Logging paths are XDG/session-scoped, files are mode-restricted, and TailLog/ListLogs apply count/line bounds.

## Rebuild checklist and known gaps

Rebuild order: canonical workspace and safeio; execution identity/lifecycle; session CAS and lease; agent authority/policy; tools and bounded outputs; provider loop; MCP namespacing/parser; recovery projections and typed reconciliation; UI/logging/resource adapters. Keep Go tests as executable invariants.

Minimum parity gaps for a smaller runtime are full providerCallID/iteration/ordinal/kind identity, argument continuity, execution cursor, effective reconciliation projection, typed user evidence, standalone/goal resolution, bounded fail-closed overflow, and separate transport/domain/evidence fields. A runtime that only blocks on a raw started row has not implemented reconciliation. A runtime that stores raw MCP structured content in a transcript has crossed a forbidden boundary. A runtime that marks command/MCP transport success as verified domain success has violated the evidence model.

Historical source names in this document are intentional exact references: internal/agent/execution.go, loop_dispatch.go, loop_authorize.go, compact.go, mcp_guidance.go, mcp_status.go; internal/permission/checker.go, destructive.go, scope_match.go; internal/safeio/publish_path.go and open_*; internal/sandbox/sandbox*.go; internal/execution/types.go; internal/db/execution_events.go, execution_hazards.go, session_state.go, reconciliation_session.go, reconciliation_groups.go, reconciliation_inspection.go, reconciliation_commit.go, standalone_reconciliation.go; internal/command/*.go; internal/resource/*.go; internal/imageasset/store.go; internal/capabilityadvisor/*.go; internal/drift/drift_test.go; and internal/logging/*.go.



## Detailed package map

agent/authority.go defines AuthorityMode and transitions among ask, plan, build, and yolo. It snapshots mode per turn so a callback cannot change authority halfway through dispatch. authority_test.go checks mode transitions and blocked effects.
agent/write_grants.go stores exact read/write grants. A grant is bound to canonical workspace/path and arguments hash; a stale or mismatched grant is refused.
agent/read_roots.go computes readable roots from workspace, project instructions, and configured leaves. It rejects overlap that would accidentally widen authority.
agent/workspace_root.go canonicalizes the workspace and project root before use. It handles missing paths and symlink roots as errors, not lexical strings.
agent/tool_admission.go validates tool names, arguments, active policy, repetition and catalog generation before the approval path. tool_admission_test.go tests malformed and unavailable calls.
agent/tool_advertisement.go builds model-visible descriptions from the narrowed policy; a tool not in the advertisement is not implicitly callable.
agent/loop_ids.go assigns stable turn/run/execution IDs and provider call IDs. These are passed to the execution ledger before dispatch.
agent/loop_limits.go contains TurnLimits validation and wall/eval/iteration/tool ceilings. loop_limits_test.go covers zero, negative, and exhausted budgets.
agent/loop_budget.go charges provider and summarizer token receipts against one logical turn.
agent/loop_provider.go handles streaming provider chunks, malformed terminal events, retries, response metadata, and context errors.
agent/loop_dispatch.go dispatchStage processes calls serially, closes later calls on cancellation, records requested/started/terminal edges, and maps tool results to output.
agent/loop_authorize.go supplies blockedToolCall, deniedToolCall, failedToolCall and cancelUndispatchedToolCalls; these close assistant tool-call edges without executing an effect.
agent/loop_errors.go classifies retryable transport/provider errors versus model/input/authority errors. Only the retryable class can repeat a provider request.
agent/continuation.go and continuation_auto.go separate explicit user continuations from host-prepared auto continuations; neither bypasses execution ledger or approval.
agent/continuation_contracts.go validates continuation permits, turn IDs, budgets and evidence. continuation tests reject stale or forged permits.
agent/checkpoint.go persists durable checkpoints and exact cursor/revision information. checkpoint_test.go verifies checkpoint failure prevents unsafe continuation.
agent/turn_receipt.go records typed turn receipts, provider/model identity, output/eval counts, and terminal/unknown states. turn_receipt_test.go checks replay and malformed receipt rejection.
agent/output.go is the interface boundary: ToolCallStart/ToolCallResult, Text, Error, Status and lifecycle metadata are emitted without making UI decide domain truth.
agent/headless_output.go and json_output.go serialize bounded event envelopes for automation. semantic_output.go projects status facts separately from raw transport.
agent/context_report.go reports context budget and source ownership. It does not expose hidden credentials or unbounded raw payloads.
agent/system.go builds the system prompt from mode, tool policy, workspace, ignore rules, memory, skill, MCP guidance and bounded loaded context.
agent/hooks.go runs optional lifecycle hooks under bounded cancellation and never grants effect authority.
agent/background.go owns background jobs/process references and cleanup. A background result is host-owned state, not an implicit shell capability.
agent/process_group_unix.go and process_group_other.go implement platform process-group termination and explicit unsupported behavior.

## More permission and safeio details

permission.Checker persists policies in the database and loads them at construction. SetPolicy rejects unknown tools/policies, Reset clears persisted policy, and SkipsApprovals/IsYolo are projections only. An allow policy still passes path/workspace/sandbox checks.
ApprovalRequest carries tool name, raw argument snapshot, argument hash, workspace, scope, preview kind, destructive consequence, and exact resource. ApprovalResponse carries decision, scope, optional grant metadata and user reason. The response cannot mutate the request.
Approval scope kinds include once, session, session-tool, session-path, session-bash-prefix, session-MCP-tool and session-MCP-server. applySessionScope only accepts a scope eligible for that exact request; broad permanent allows are unsupported.
permission/workspace_rules.go loads bounded JSON rules from the workspace authority file, validates exact tool/path/prefix/MCP names, and rejects unknown fields. workspace_rules_export.go creates a redacted public projection.
safeio/regular_file.go refuses nonregular source/destination entries and checks mode/type. safeio/open_nofollow_posix.go uses O_NOFOLLOW and safeio/open_follow_posix.go permits following only after canonical containment.
safeio/open_within_posix.go walks parent components through directory descriptors, preventing an attacker from swapping a parent directory after lexical validation.
safeio/publish_path.go writes a private temp file, fsyncs/validates bytes, checks pinned parent/file identity, renames atomically, and cleans temp state. It does not use an unvalidated absolute-path delete.
safeio/lock.go provides a process/external lease abstraction; flock/fcntl implementations return busy without waiting and close releases the lock. lock tests exercise two processes and bad lock objects.
safeio/open_within_other.go is conservative on platforms without descriptor primitives; it rejects operations that cannot establish the boundary rather than silently using weak path checks.

## More tool lifecycle details

read and grep never infer authority from a server response. Their path resolver applies workspace root, symlink evaluation and ignore exclusions before opening. Directory traversal checks context periodically so cancellation is responsive.
write uses complete-content semantics; the approval preview contains old/new bounded content or an omitted reason. Existing content is reread before commit so a concurrent edit is rejected.
edit's replacement engine counts exact matches before mutation. replace_all must be explicit; literal replacement uses a callback so replacement metacharacters do not interpolate. Patch mode verifies old line ranges and context.
remove distinguishes missing with force from an actual failure. recursive is required for directories; workspace root and excluded sensitive roots remain protected.
copy reads source through safe descriptors, creates destination parent as allowed, preserves bounded content semantics, and rejects copying through a symlink target. move checks both source and destination and refuses root moves.
bash uses a shell deliberately because the schema is a shell command; the shell is still under executable resolution, environment sanitization, timeout/process-group cleanup and sandbox policy. It does not claim OS sandbox on unsupported platforms.
bash_output is read-only because it can only address a process ID previously returned by this session's bash. The buffer cursor advances; repeated reads are suppressed to prevent model loops.
ask_user's yes_no default is no; skip/empty is a declined answer. single requires at least two valid choices, while freetext accepts bounded text. It cannot grant filesystem permission.
load_skill is progressive: exact catalog lookup precedes body loading, and loading changes prompt context only for the current agent, not global policy.
consult_experts executes tool-free child profiles. Their text is advisory and must be verified by the parent; model overrides are exact inventory names and cannot create remote access.
exists reports type/size/permissions only through a bounded projection; it does not expose arbitrary file content.

## Durable records and crash semantics

Requested is recorded before an approval request is shown when the call identity is known. approval_requested, approved, started, and terminal edges are immutable. A missing terminal edge after started is an uncertainty, not failure or automatic retry.
For a timeout/cancellation after dispatch, the host records cancelled or outcome_unknown according to whether an external effect could have happened. A failed transport after dispatch is also potentially unknown; the backend result is evidence, not permission to retry.
Raw execution rows never carry argument bodies; they carry argument SHA-256 and bounded result receipt/detail. Exact replay compares every immutable field, including result hashes and receipt.
The effective projection groups latest events by execution ID, orders by durable event ID, and applies reconciliation resolutions only after validating target event hash, effect class, item payload hash and evidence digest.
A completed effectful event newer than the saved execution cursor is a projection-repair hazard even though its backend outcome is known. It must be projected into restored session state before continuation.
Goal-owned hazards and goal-less standalone hazards are separate. Goal-owned reconciliation requires a blocked outcome-unknown goal and a complete turn group; standalone evidence yields a closed host context but does not clear a goal.
Member resolution never clears the parent blocker. The parent resolution requires every member, validates the group/member set and snapshot cursor, then atomically patches goal state and execution cursor.
Commit paths acquire the external execution-session lease before SQLite transaction. They use session revision CAS, immutable control item/resolution triggers, and exact replay read-back after ambiguous commit.
Inspection is read-only and returns tokens (session revision, event ID, execution ID, argument digest, item ID). Apply must echo those tokens; a changed lifecycle row or session revision fails closed.
